title: One Corporate Travel Programme to One Contracting Entity
content:
One contracting company holds exactly one corporate travel programme, and a second programme is never opened for the same legal entity. A group of companies with separate legal entities holds one programme per entity, and the entities are billed separately even where one address administers them all. Where a company has somehow acquired two programmes, the older is kept, the seats and the balance of the younger are merged into it, and the younger is closed. A traveller is not a programme: travellers occupy seats on a programme and hold their own personal club membership entirely separately.

| Basis | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| Corporate Travel Programmes held by one contracting legal entity | 1 |
| Of two programmes on one entity, the one kept | The older |

## The rule read against what is presented

| What is presented | What is held under the Corporate Travel Programmes |
| --- | --- |
| One legal entity, however many offices or travellers it has | One programme |
| A group of several separate legal entities | One programme for each entity, each billed separately |
| Several entities administered from one address | The count is unaffected: each entity keeps its own programme and its own bill |
| A named traveller | No programme of their own: a seat on a programme, and a personal Wanderlane Traveller Club membership held entirely separately |

## Where a second programme has been opened on one entity

Two programmes standing on one legal entity are reduced to one. The older of the two is the programme kept. The seats of the younger and the balance of the younger are merged into the older, and the younger is closed.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical)

**A holding company and two subsidiaries, three registered legal entities, all administered from one head office address.** Three programmes are held, one to each entity, and each entity is billed separately. The shared administering address does not join them into one holding.

**A traveller asks to hold a programme in their own name alongside their employer's.** A traveller is not a contracting company. They occupy a seat on the employer's programme, and their personal club membership stands entirely apart from that programme.
